title: QUIC Connection Migration Hosted Proof Lane Verification
verification_method: Requirement-home tests, helper dry-run planning, workflow review, artifact inspection, and hosted workflow dispatch when external evidence is required.
preconditions: The external `quic-interop-runner` checkout includes `quic-go` and `msquic` peer slots.
Hosted dispatch has Docker Engine 28.1 or later, Python 3.12, and Wireshark packet-analysis tools available.
The repo-local helper remains responsible for image replacement, runner invocation, inventory output, and per-cell artifact capture.
scope: Verify that the repository exposes a manual advisory hosted proof lane for server-role connectionmigration against quic-go and msquic, without promoting blocked cells or changing ordinary CI gates.
procedure: Review `.github/workflows/interop-runner-handshake.yml` and confirm the `connectionmigration-server-proof` profile is `workflow_dispatch` only.
Confirm the profile includes server-role matrix cells against `quic-go` and `msquic` for `connectionmigration`.
Confirm every matrix cell invokes `scripts/interop/Invoke-QuicInteropRunner.ps1` with matrix-provided role, local implementation slot, peer slot, testcase, timeout, and artifact root.
Confirm each cell uploads a distinct artifact bundle with `if: always()`.
Run the focused requirement-home tests for `REQ-QUIC-INT-0018` and `REQ-QUIC-INT-0022`.
Run representative helper dry-run plans for server-role quic-go and msquic connectionmigration cells.

When external evidence is required, dispatch `gh workflow run interop-runner-handshake.yml --repo incursa/quic-dotnet --ref main -f coverage_profile=connectionmigration-server-proof` and inspect each uploaded `runner-report.json` plus selected output logs.
expected_result: The repository configuration provides an opt-in hosted proof lane that can collect per-cell artifacts for Incursa.Quic as the server role against quic-go and msquic for the connectionmigration cell, while keeping the major-peer-matrix profile and HTTP/3 out of scope.
status_summary: Planned for hosted execution. The repository now has the dedicated connectionmigration proof lane and the helper inventory already classifies connectionmigration as supported/executed. The latest local migration proof still shows the quic-go cell failing, which keeps the msquic comparison as the next GitHub-hosted trace target. Full SpecTrace core validation remains blocked by the current baseline and is not claimed as passing by this artifact.

supplemental_sections.heading: Deferred Coverage
supplemental_sections.content: `http3` remains out of scope. `v2`, `rebind-port`, and `rebind-addr` remain prerequisite-blocked under the non-HTTP/3 inventory. `connectionmigration` now has a dedicated hosted proof lane, but the lane itself still needs live corroboration before any support claim changes.
